title: epiworldRcalibrate
format: gfm

A generic framework for calibrating epidemic and agent-based models.

## Core idea

Every calibration method is represented by the same simple S3 object:

```r
calibrator_example <- list(
  pre_process = function(x, ...) { ... },
  run = function(x, ...) { ... },
  post_process = function(x, ...) { ... },
  type = "SIR"
) |>
  structure(class = "calibrator")
```

All methods are called through:

```r
calibrate(daily_cases, calibrator, ...)
```

This keeps the **epidemic model** independent of the **calibration method**.

## Three-step organization

```text
R/01_simulation.R     data generation/import
R/02_training.R       training + calibrator definitions
R/03_test_compare.R   calibration + testing + benchmark comparisons
```

## Built-in training-data support

The package currently generates training banks for:

- SIR
- SEIR

For other models such as SIRH/SEIRD, users may provide their own training
data or plug in their own simulator.

## Calibration methods

The package currently demonstrates:

- BiLSTM
- ABC-MCMC
- ABC-SMC
- Nelder-Mead
- Differential Evolution

A user can add any new method by creating another four-field `calibrator`
object; `calibrate()` itself does not change.

See [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md) for complete examples.


## Step-by-step documentation

For the complete copy/paste workflow, see [STEP_BY_STEP_GUIDE.md](STEP_BY_STEP_GUIDE.md).


## Run SIR and SEIR end-to-end

To actually generate SIR/SEIR training banks, train both BiLSTM models, and
produce validation/test results, open:

```text
examples/RUN_SIR_SEIR_BILSTM.Rmd
```

and Knit it.

At the top of the file:

```r
FULL_RUN <- FALSE
```

runs a small pipeline test. Change to:

```r
FULL_RUN <- TRUE
```

for the current full settings (5,000 SIR simulations, 20,000 SEIR simulations,
100 epochs for each model).

The official Getting Started vignette remains lightweight documentation and
does not run the expensive full training workflow during package checks.
